search_bias: benchmark-design and measurement-validity first; judge meta-evaluation, process verification, downstream-valid evaluator testing, prompt/format robustness, and uncertainty/reliability diagnostics

new_sources_checked.title: Time to REFLECT: Can We Trust LLM Judges for Evidence-based Research Agents?
AgentProcessBench: Diagnosing Step-Level Process Quality in Tool-Using Agents
Judging the Judges: A Systematic Evaluation of Bias Mitigation Strategies in LLM-as-a-Judge Pipelines
AgentRewardBench: Evaluating Automatic Evaluations of Web Agent Trajectories
JudgeSense: A Benchmark for Prompt Sensitivity in LLM-as-a-Judge Systems
Who can we trust? LLM-as-a-jury for Comparative Assessment

candidate_findings.mechanism: Meta-evaluate research-agent judges with verified clean-vs-localized-corruption pairs, score failure detection by category, and combine fine-grained local judging with holistic checks for context-dependent failures rather than trusting one aggregate judge score.
candidate_findings.evidence: REFLECT constructs 140 reasoning, 132 tool-use, and 200 outcome perturbations with localized edits and human validation (inter-annotator kappa 0.86). Pointwise judge best overall accuracies are only 45.7% for reasoning, 54.5% for tool use, and 47.5% for report quality. Fine-grained judging improves over holistic judging across the reported model/protocol cells by +2.8 to +34.3 percentage points, while holistic judging remains better for some global-context failure types such as shallow reflection/topical misalignment.
candidate_findings.quantitative: N=472 controlled perturbations (140 reasoning, 132 tool-use, 200 outcome); kappa=0.86; best holistic pointwise overall 45.7% reasoning / 54.5% tool / 47.5% report; fine-grained minus holistic +2.8 to +34.3 pp in Table 2
candidate_findings.scope: deep-research-agent trajectories and reports under controlled localized interventions
candidate_findings.uncertainty: Controlled perturbations improve causal diagnosis but do not exhaust naturally occurring or interactive failures; exact Best-of-N numeric accuracies/cost frontier remain to be extracted.

candidate_findings.mechanism: For tool-using agents, evaluate both dense step correctness and earliest critical-error localization; keep a neutral/exploratory label, and combine process signals with outcome signals for selection rather than treating either alone as sufficient.
candidate_findings.evidence: AgentProcessBench contains 1,000 trajectories and 8,509 human-labeled steps with 89.1% inter-annotator agreement. Its strongest reported model reaches 81.6% StepAcc but only 65.8% FirstErrAcc, exposing a substantial localization gap. On the top 25% longest trajectories, StepAcc falls 3.8-13.49 points and FirstErrAcc falls 10.79-21.67 points. In GAIA Best-of-8, two-stage outcome->process selection improves over outcome-only for every listed generator: 37.7->43.4, 35.9->50.9, 47.2->49.1, 56.6->64.2, and 56.6->58.5; oracle Pass@8 is 77.4%.
candidate_findings.quantitative: 1,000 trajectories; 8,509 steps; 89.1% IAA; strongest 81.6% StepAcc vs 65.8% FirstErrAcc; long-horizon drops 3.8-13.49 StepAcc and 10.79-21.67 FirstErrAcc; Best-of-8 two-stage gains up to +15.0 pp
candidate_findings.scope: realistic tool-augmented trajectories spanning HotPotQA, GAIA, BFCL, and tau2-Bench
candidate_findings.uncertainty: Error-propagation labeling is evaluator-dependent: removing it improved DeepSeek-V3.2 two-stage selection by +3.7 pp but hurt DeepSeek-V3.2-Thinking by -13.2 pp and Gemini-3-Flash by -5.7 pp. Protocol choice requires ablation rather than assumption.

candidate_findings.mechanism: Calibrate judge protocols to the actual judge/task bias profile using controlled counterfactual pairs and cost-aware strategy selection; do not apply position-swap/CoT/ensemble universally.
candidate_findings.evidence: A TMLR 2026 study compares nine strategies across five judges, three benchmarks, and a 375-pair controlled set. In its current-model setup, style bias (0.10-0.76, markdown preference) dominates position bias (<=0.04), while verbosity preference is model-dependent. The best tested configuration is Gemini 2.5 Flash with Combined Budget at 71.0% agreement and kappa 0.549 at about $0.001/eval, versus the best frontier setup Claude Sonnet 4 at 69.5% and about $0.015/eval. Holm-Bonferroni-surviving gains include Claude S8 +11.5 pp, Flash S8 +7.5 pp, and Claude S5 +7.3 pp.
candidate_findings.quantitative: style bias 0.10-0.76; position <=0.04; best agreement 71.0%, kappa=0.549, ~$0.001/eval; ~15x cheaper than 69.5% frontier setup; significant gains +7.3 to +11.5 pp
candidate_findings.scope: pairwise text judging on MT-Bench, LLMBar, and controlled formatting/length/model-origin tests
candidate_findings.uncertainty: Bias rankings conflict with other protocols such as JudgeSense's pairwise always-A behavior; therefore bias is measurement-design and task dependent, not a universal property of a model.

candidate_findings.mechanism: Validate agent evaluators against expert-labeled trajectories across heterogeneous environments and multiple dimensions (success, side effects, repetition), and report precision/recall/F1 by benchmark rather than treating benchmark rule checks as ground truth.
candidate_findings.evidence: AgentRewardBench has 1,302 trajectories across five web benchmarks and four agent LLMs, with expert labels and 89.3% inter-annotator agreement on success. No single LLM judge excels across all benchmarks. Official rule-based evaluation has overall precision 83.8%, recall 55.9%, F1 67.1; a simplified GPT-4o judge using final accessibility-tree input reports precision 69.8%, recall 83.1%, F1 75.9. The paper finds rule-based evaluators systematically underreport successful trajectories.
candidate_findings.quantitative: 1,302 trajectories; 5 benchmarks; 4 agent models; 89.3% success-label IAA; rule F1 67.1 vs simplified GPT-4o A11Y F1 75.9
candidate_findings.scope: web-agent trajectory success evaluation across AssistantBench, VisualWebArena, WebArena, WorkArena, WorkArena++
candidate_findings.uncertainty: Expert labels are environment-specific and the best precision/recall tradeoff depends on downstream use (e.g. rejection fine-tuning vs monitoring).

candidate_findings.mechanism: Treat judge-prompt wording as a measurement variable: test verdict invariance under validated semantically equivalent prompt paraphrases and separate true judge instability from polarity/order artifacts.
candidate_findings.evidence: JudgeSense evaluates nine judges on 494 validated paraphrase pairs. Coherence JSS ranges from 0.389 to 0.992; factuality appears around 0.63 before correcting a polarity-inverted template and rises to about 0.9 afterward. Pairwise preference/relevance shows degenerate always-A behavior in 8 of 9 judges, demonstrating that apparent stability can itself be an order artifact. Model scale does not predict consistency.
candidate_findings.quantitative: 494 validated paraphrase pairs; coherence JSS 0.389-0.992; factuality ~0.63 before polarity correction and ~0.9 after; always-A in 8/9 pairwise judges
candidate_findings.scope: prompt-sensitivity meta-evaluation for factuality, coherence, preference, and relevance judging
candidate_findings.uncertainty: The always-A result conflicts with a separate current-model controlled-bias study that reports small position bias; differences in task construction and prompt format must be reconciled before generalization.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Fine-grained judging alone is always superior
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: REFLECT shows strong average/local gains but holistic judging can better expose failures requiring global context, accumulated evidence, or overall intent. Use mixed granularity.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: A single step-accuracy metric is sufficient for process evaluators
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: AgentProcessBench shows first-error localization is materially harder than aggregate step labeling, and long trajectories disproportionately degrade FirstErrAcc.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Error-propagation labels are universally correct for tool-agent process evaluation
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: AgentProcessBench ablation is evaluator-dependent: removing propagation improves one evaluator by +3.7 pp but degrades stronger evaluators by -5.7 to -13.2 pp in Best-of-8 selection.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Rule-based environment success should be treated as ground truth for web-agent evaluator training
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: AgentRewardBench finds high precision but low recall for official rules and systematic underreporting of expert-defined success.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Position swap is the dominant universal judge mitigation
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: A 2026 TMLR controlled study finds negligible position bias but large style bias for its tested modern judges, while JudgeSense reports severe always-A behavior under different pairwise protocols. The safe conclusion is protocol-specific measurement, not a universal ranking of biases.
